newsitem.title: USA: Georgia Vogtle unit reduces power for repair.
newsitem.headline: Georgia Vogtle unit reduces power for repair.

text.p: Georgia Power Co's 1,162 megawatt Vogtle nuclear power unit 2 reduced electricity output to 65 percent of capacity for a repair but was expected to return to full capacity by Friday, a spokeswoman said.
Power output at the Waynesboro, Ga., unit was cut Tuesday for examination of a feed pump vibration, spokeswoman Loretto Stevens said Wednesday.
The pump was being replaced and the unit "should be back at 100 percent by Friday," Stevens said.
Unit production was not expected to drop below 65 percent, she said.
The Vogtle plant, made up of two 1,162 megawatt units, is operated and 45.7 percent owned by Georgia Power, a subsidiary of Southern Co.
Oglethorpe Power Corp has a 30 percent interest in the Vogtle plant, with the Municipal Electric Authority of Georgia holding 22.7 percent and the City of Dalton, Ga. holding 1.6 percent.
The Vogtle unit 1 continued to operate normally at 100 percent of capacity.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
